memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: And fire came out from the Lord and consumed the 250 men who were offering the incense. The Lord said to Moses, "Tell Eleazar son of Aaron, the priest, to take the censers out of the fire and scatter the coals some distance away, for the censers are holy — the censers of the men who sinned at the cost of their lives. Hammer the censers into sheets to overlay the altar, for they were presented before the Lord and have become holy. Let them be a sign to the Israelites." — Num 16:35-38 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The 250 leaders who dared to offer incense — a priestly act reserved for those God appointed — are consumed by fire from the Lord. Their rebellion had been an attempt to approach God on their own terms, seizing a holiness He had not granted them. And approaching a holy God wrongly proved fatal.

There is a solemn truth here that runs through all of Scripture: we do not get to come to God however we please. He is holy, and He appoints the way of approach. The 250 assumed that sincerity and self-appointment were enough. But God had provided one way to draw near, through the priesthood He established, and to bypass it was to court destruction. Good intentions are no substitute for coming God's way.

Then comes a striking command: the censers of these men, having been presented before the Lord, are hammered into a covering for the altar — a permanent warning to future generations. God took the very instruments of rebellion and turned them into a lasting reminder of the seriousness of approaching Him rightly.

This points us, by contrast, to the wonder of the gospel. We could never approach a holy God on our own terms or by our own merit; the attempt can only end in judgment. But God Himself has provided the one and only way to come near — not a human priesthood, but His own Son. Jesus is our great High Priest, and through Him alone we draw near with confidence. We do not have to invent our own path to God, nor should we. The way is opened, freely, in Christ. Come through Him, and you are welcomed, not consumed.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you try to approach God on your own terms, or His?
2. Why are sincerity and good intentions not enough to approach a holy God?
3. How does Jesus being your High Priest give you confidence to draw near?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You are holy, and I cannot come to You on my own terms or by my own merit. Thank You that You have opened the one true way through Jesus, my great High Priest. I draw near through Him alone, and in Him I am welcomed. Amen.
